Row.Text: Re-dealable Leader Abilities, Attributes, and Start Biases

Re-deals leader abilities, attributes and start biases for a new game. Swap whole abilities or whole leaders, or break abilities into their bullet points and deal them out, and switch any of the three off for a game on equal footing. It's built for multiplayer through the game's own lobby, and the game's leader screens show what each leader got, with a line for where they like to start.
Only the host can change these settings. You'll see them here as the host sets them.
This pool is empty. A slot set to Random from this pool gets an ordinary random leader.
You don't have any of the listed modded leaders installed and turned on, so modded leaders play as their mods ship them.
Mixes up leader abilities, attributes and start biases for this game. The leader screens show what each leader got.
Where leaders and civilizations like to start. Off: the map places everyone without leaning toward any terrain, whatever the mode.
Off: leaders play without their abilities, and attributes and start biases still follow the mode.
Off: leaders play without attributes, and each leader gets all twelve diplomatic actions the attributes would have unlocked, so everyone has the same set.
Each human player keeps the leader they picked as the game ships it: ability, attributes, start bias and personality. The AI leaders are re-dealt among themselves.

A leader switched off here plays as the game ships it. Only the leaders in the game are re-dealt among themselves, including the ones picked for Random slots. In an online game, if another player leaves their own slot on Random, every leader still switched on goes into the deal, so bonuses can come from leaders who aren't playing.

Lets the abilities of listed modded leaders into the deal. The leader's mod has to be installed and turned on and pass a check of its files at setup; other modded leaders play as their mods ship them.

Lets the attributes of listed modded leaders into the deal. The leader's mod has to be installed and turned on and pass a check of its files at setup; other modded leaders play as their mods ship them.

Lets the start biases of listed modded leaders into the deal. The leader's mod has to be installed and turned on and pass a check of its files at setup; other modded leaders play as their mods ship them.
The listed modded leaders you have installed. A leader you switch off here plays as its mod ships it.
Pick the leaders for this pool. A player slot set to Random from pool 1 gets one of them when the game starts, and two slots never get the same leader.
Pick the leaders for this pool. A player slot set to Random from pool 2 gets one of them when the game starts, and two slots never get the same leader.
How an AI leader behaves: its agendas and the civilizations it likes to pick in each age.
How the split modes hand out the pieces of each ability.
When you get to see the other leaders' abilities, attributes and start biases for this game.

The same number with the same settings and leaders gives the same deal, so you can share it and a friend can play the same roll. Setup picks a new number each time it opens, and the number shows on the loading screen.
Leaders play as the game ships them. The Off switches still apply.
Each leader takes another leader's whole ability, two random attributes, and a start bias rolled from scratch. The three aren't tied to each other.
Each leader takes another leader's whole package: ability, attributes and start bias together. Amina might play with Pachacuti's mountain bonuses and start beside mountains.

Abilities are broken into their bullet points and dealt out with the attributes. Each leader's start bias comes from the pieces they got, so whoever holds Pachacuti's mountain bullets starts near mountains. Until a leader's bullets have been checked by hand, that leader's ability is dealt whole.

Abilities and attributes are dealt out in pieces as in Split abilities, matched starts, and start biases are rolled from scratch. Until a leader's bullets have been checked by hand, that leader's ability is dealt whole.
Mixed up the way How leaders are re-dealt says.
Switched off for all leaders, for a game on equal footing. A leader kept as chosen keeps theirs.
Each AI leader keeps its own agendas and civilization picks, and still plays the bonuses it was dealt.
Agendas and civilization picks move with the ability, so the AI acts like the leader whose bonuses it holds. In the split modes they come from the leader who gave it the most pieces.
Whole personalities are dealt out to random leaders on their own, apart from the abilities.
Each leader's pieces add up to about the same strength, so one leader can't end up with all the strong bullets.
Pieces go out at random, strong or weak, the way the cards fall.
The leader screens show everyone's deal from setup on.
You see your own deal at setup. Another leader's deal shows in the diplomacy panel and the Civilopedia once you've met them.
A random leader from Leader pool 1, picked when the game starts. If the pool is empty or used up, the slot gets an ordinary random leader.
A random leader from Leader pool 2, picked when the game starts. If the pool is empty or used up, the slot gets an ordinary random leader.
Starts anywhere the map puts them
Starts where this map places them; it doesn't use start biases
Leader abilities are off for this game.
You haven't met this leader yet.
Fewer than two leaders were left to re-deal here, so this part stays as the game ships it.
Another mod changed the leaders, so this deal is different from the one the setup screen showed.

switched off in Modded leaders to re-deal
